summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 6, part 94) in which the narrator, Cas Russell, is questioned by a woman named Jones, apparently a federal agent, after Professor Halliday has been rescued. Jones pushes Cas to reveal her real name, and Cas deflects with sarcasm, insisting that Cas Russell is her real name and refusing to cooperate with suspicion. Cas reasons that she is safer if the authorities care about her only in relation to Halliday, and the scene ends with Jones demanding a detailed account of what happened inside.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, narrator Cas Russell is interrogated by agent Jones about her identity and the rescue of Professor Halliday.
key_facts: Jones calls the narrator 'Cas Russell' and the narrator notes that being brown and female made it easy for authorities to identify her.
The narrator thinks the authorities would have had a much longer list of names to check if she were a six-foot-tall white man.
Jones tells the narrator she is 'a fingernail's width away from going from witness to perpetrator.'
Jones asks for the narrator's 'real name,' and the narrator insists 'Cas Russell is my real name.'
The narrator offers to take a polygraph, claiming she could control her physiological responses but is telling the truth in this case.
The narrator says that burning an alias every job would prevent her from building a client base.
The narrator sarcastically gives the name 'Bridget Twitwaffle' when pressed.
The narrator reasons that if the Feds only cared about her in reference to Halliday, it might be a very good thing for her.
When asked what happened, the narrator answers that she 'tracked down Professor Halliday and rescued her.'
Jones demands a detailed account of every event from the narrator.
